strategy_statement: One engine signs every order of the three wallets (per-wallet sequential salt counter, timestamp/metadata/builder 0, daily 01:00 UTC restart) [VALIDATE-only]. Each wallet keeps a ladder of BUY quotes (several 500-share rungs plus a 100-share level on 10-31; 62/12 or 250/50 on other days) on both outcomes of BTC 5m and BTC 15m Up/Down windows (and other crypto Up/Down markets), each side on its own; the three wallets post the same quote within 20 ms (bursts of exactly 2-3 adds), and every rung is cancelled and re-posted about once a second at a new price [hypothesis: live development block 10-31, raw book]. The ladder sits about 7.5 cents below the token's mid on average (q = -0.055 + 0.69 mid + 0.25 futures fair), deepens near the end of the window and above fair 0.8, and moves with the Binance USD-M futures mid within 50-250 ms when it moves (85-97% of re-posts), otherwise with the Polymarket touch (89%); Bybit, OKX, Coinbase, Binance spot, Hyperliquid and Chainlink explain the re-posts less [hypothesis: live]. It is filled when the market comes down to one of its rungs or a rung reaches the best bid of the token the futures fair says is underpriced; its filled orders were posted 0-5 s before the match (46% within 1 s vs 6% at random) [exam-verified partially: side 0.655, price 0.688 on the fill tape]. Partial fills are re-posted as remainders [hypothesis: live]. It holds to resolution and sometimes taker-buys the under-held complement to the exact imbalance and merges (2-4% of PnL) [VALIDATE-only]. It is not settlement-informed (its late inventory follows the true outcome in 60% of proxy-disagreement windows vs 73-85% for the market) and earns almost nothing from rewards ($0.81) and 8% from rebates. Profit: the spread from dispersed and large takers on a futures-anchored ladder refreshed faster than the average maker's; in busy periods mostly from buying both outcomes cheaply at different moments (+11% on paired dollars). Not decoded: which windows are switched on, and the rung prices to a tick (a flexible model of public inputs gets 21% within a tick, like a trivial anchor), hence when a rung is at the touch.

selection.description: one engine over crypto Up/Down; BTC 5m = 78% of VALIDATE fills / 69% of abs PnL, BTC 5m+15m 87% / 89% (STUDY 54% / 56% and 63% / 75%); the same 500/100 quote stream runs in BTC 15m live; BTC 5m on/off is a runtime switch with no public correlate yet.

timing.description: continuous re-signing: 500/100 quotes are cancelled and re-added about every 0.4-0.7 s (re-add 15 ms after the cancel), ~17 signed orders/s per wallet; near-touch requote direction follows Binance USD-M futures mid moves of the previous 50-250 ms (96-97%) and the Polymarket touch between them (89%) [live development block 10-31, shared size class: hypothesis]; its filled orders were posted 0-5 s before the match (46% within 1 s); exposed to moves of the last ~0.25-1.5 s (STUDY ms clocks).

side.description: Up and Down quoted independently; it is filled on the side where its futures-fair quote reaches the touch: VALIDATE 0.663 vs 0.613 activity baseline; exam round 1 0.655 vs 0.600.

price.description: rule: last clean print - 0.01 (within one tick 0.709 VALIDATE, exam 0.688; BTC 15m 0.656-0.666). Live (hypothesis): a ladder of 500-share rungs about 7.5 c below the token mid (q = -0.055 + 0.69 mid + 0.25 futures fair, residual MAD 0.037), deeper near the end; rung prices are not predictable to a tick from public inputs (held-out 20.8% vs anchor 21.3%).

size.description: runtime size class with a one-fifth second level (500/100 on Saturday 10-31 14:00 UTC; 62/12 or 250/50 on other days), several 500 rungs per side live; partially filled orders are re-posted with the remainder (492.44, 76.38, ...); size does not depend on the edge.

exit.description: holds to resolution; taker-buys the under-held complement (72-83% of its taker buys) sized to the imbalance or one fifth, pair cost 1.06-1.12, then merges in 17-51% of those windows; small PnL weight (2-4%); maker-maker pairs are 90% of paired shares.
